data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Aikathos, meaning pure or clean. In the New Testament, Katharina is the Greek form of the name Catherine, which means pure. Kathia is a beautiful and meaningful name for a baby girl in Christian traditions. The name Kathia carries the meaning “Pure, Clean” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Kathia usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, clean and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: קתיה
in_hebrew.meaning: קתיה משמעות השם טוהר הנפש וקרבת לב
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קתיה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו טוהר הנפש וקרבת לב. השם קתיה קשור למילה היוונית 'קatharos' שפירושה טהור. השם נמצא בשימוש בקרב הנוצרים כסמל לטוהר הלב והנפש. בהקשר התנ"כי, השם קתיה מזכיר את החשיבות של טוהר הלב והנפש ביחסים עם אלוהים.

in_greek.name: Καθεία
in_greek.long_meaning: Καθεία είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'καθαρός' που σημαίνει καθαρότητα. Το όνομα Καθεία συνδέεται με την έννοια της αγιότητας και της καθαρότητας της ψυχής. Στην πρώιμη χριστιανική εκκλησία, το όνομα Καθεία ήταν σύμβολο της πνευματικής καθαρότητας και της εγγύτητας με τον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Cathia
in_latin.long_meaning: Cathia est nomen christianum quod ex graeco origine trahit, significans puritatem cordis et spiritus. Nomen Cathia coniungitur cum notione puritatis et sanctitatis. In ecclesia christiana primitiva, nomen Cathia erat symbolum puritatis spiritualis et propinquitas ad Deum.

Historically, the name has been used in Christian traditions to signify spiritual cleanliness and closeness to God. The name Kathia is associated with virtues such as innocence, sincerity, and devotion. In modern Christian cultures, Kathia remains a popular name for girls, reflecting the enduring significance of purity and spiritual integrity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kathia has a rich history and cultural significance in the Christian world. It is derived from the Greek name Aikathos, and in Christian tradition, it is most commonly associated with Saint Catherine of Alexandria. She was a prominent early Christian martyr who, according to legend, was tortured on a spiked wheel before being beheaded. Images of Saint Catherine often depict her standing on a wheel, which has come to symbolize her strength and resilience in the face of persecution.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kathia carries a deep spiritual significance in Christian traditions. Derived from the Greek word for pure, it reminds us of the essential purity and holiness that lies within each person. It is a name that encourages us to strive for spiritual growth and to live in accordance with the teachings of Christ. Additionally, it is a reminder of the purity and sanctity of God's love and the importance of keeping our hearts and minds pure and open to His will.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kathia, derived from the Greek name Aikathia, meaning pure, signifies a soul deeply rooted in spiritual purity and divine wisdom. It symbolizes a life dedicated to seeking inner truth, illuminated by the light of Christ.

historical_references.reference: According to legend, Saint Katharine of Alexandria was a Christian virgin martyr who lived during the late 3rd or early 4th century. She was famed for her purity, learning, and eloquence. Her feast day is celebrated on November 25 in the Western Christian liturgical calendar, and on the first Sunday of November in the Eastern Christian liturgical calendar.

Another Saint Katharine, also known as Catherine of Siena, was born in 1347 in Siena, Italy. She was a prominent member of the lay Third Order of Saint Dominic, and was canonized as a saint in 1461. She was noted for her mystical experiences, writings, and her role as a counselor to popes and other religious leaders.
